title: Robust Parallel Diffusion Sampling via Dynamic Jacobian Bandwidth
claim: Our method keeps the linear system well-conditioned and converges in far fewer iterations and more smoothly than competing parallel samplers.
layout: 3 line-plot panels in a row, shared legend on top, shaded bands
description: A single row of three line plots with a shared legend above for ROPA and the baselines ParaSolver, ParaTAA and ParaDIGMS. ROPA is drawn in dark indigo, and the baselines are in teal-to-green shades. Panel (a) plots the log10 Jacobian condition number against normalized time. The baselines are noisy and high, between about 5.5 and 6.5. ROPA stays flat and low, near 4.5 down to 4. Shaded green and blue bands mark each group's range, and a pink strip marks the early timesteps. Panel (b) is a CDF of convergence ratio against the number of iterations. ROPA's curve rises steeply and reaches 1.0 by about 10 iterations. The baselines rise slowly and plateau at 0.8 or below. Panel (c) plots trajectory curvature against normalized time. ROPA oscillates in a narrow band near zero, while the baselines fluctuate widely. The eye goes first to ROPA's distinct curves.
caption: ROPA Performance Analysis. (a) Estimated Jacobian conditioning showing improved numerical stability. (b) Convergence
abstract: Recent years have witnessed significant progress in developing effective diffusion models. Parallel sampling is a promising recent approach that reformulates the sequential denoising process as solving a system of nonlinear equations, and it can be combined with other acceleration techniques. However, current progress is limited by the trade-off between high fidelity and computational efficiency. This paper addresses the challenge of scaling to high-dimensional, multi-modal generation. Specifically, we present ROPA (Robust Parallel Diffusion Sampling), which takes into account the properties of the denoising process and solves the linear system using adaptive local sparsity to achieve stable parallel sampling. Extensive experiments demonstrate ROPA’s effectiveness: it significantly accelerates sampling across diverse image and video diffusion models, achieving up to $2.9\times$ speedup with eight core, an improvement of 20.8\% over baselines without sacrificing sample quality. ROPA enables parallel sampling methods to provide a solid foundation for real-time, high-fidelity diffusion generation.
